subject: Image Overlays

description: A three-column robot-kit comparison poster drawn with p5.js whose columns are percentage zones: hover and click to open each kit's summary and facts, or answer which-column quiz questions scored on the first try.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Comparing items across the columns of a comparison poster
learningObjectives: The learner will compare three items across the same attributes by exploring the columns of a poster, and will identify which column matches a described property.
prerequisites: Poster Column Zones, Zone Summary and Facts, and Explore Mode and Quiz Mode sections of Chapter 10

accessibility.notes: describe() names the selected column and its summary; poster text is also available as panel text

controls.label: Explore
controls.purpose: Hover to highlight a column and click to open its summary and facts

controls.label: Quiz Me
controls.purpose: Ask the five which-column questions in random order

controls.label: Show zone edges
controls.purpose: Reveal the x1, y1, x2, y2 percentages of each zone

controls.label: Base Bot, WiFi Bot, Display Bot
controls.purpose: Rectangular hit testing from percentage zones

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Poster column zones with explore mode, quiz mode and first-try scoring
keyQuestions: Which attributes do all three kits share?
What single attribute sets each kit apart?
Why must each quiz question be true of exactly one column?
commonMisconceptions: A poster's printed text and its overlay facts can be edited independently
A quiz score that counts only correct answers measures first-try understanding
Wider zones must hold more important items
assessmentOpportunities: First-try score over five which-column questions
